content:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a weird spike in provisional charges this morning from a background embed job. It routed through `background-priority` and ate ~1.2M tokens charged to cust-1234. Anyone seen this pattern?
aj: Did it overlap with any streaming requests? Background embeds should route low-priority and use the system pool, not customer's quota.
devon: quick FYI: router has a new heuristic from last week: `if has_embed && route_hint == 'urgent' -> background-priority` — intended for dedupe bursts. Could be the culprit.
irene: I remember that PR. It was to reduce latency for duplicate embeds. @devon can you drop the exact snippet?
devon: sure — pasted below:
```
// router patch 2026-03-10
if (request.meta?.embed && request.headers['x-route-hint'] === 'urgent') {
  route = 'background-priority';
  // preserve headers for continuity
  forwardHeaders(request, ['x-route-owner', 'x-correlation-id']);
}
```
maria: Node billing shows tokens attributed to cust-1234's API key rather than system pool. That attribution switch is the problem.
billing-bot: Alert: provisional_charge created for cust-1234 (1,200,045 tokens). Ticket #BILL-842.
aj: Two CFs here: 1) routing allowed background to take burst capacity (chargeable), 2) accounting uses `route_owner` header — if that gets forwarded from client, tokens get attributed to them.
devon: ah — we started preserving `x-route-owner` for toolcall continuity in the same change. That means an internal background request can accidentally carry customer ownership.
irene: proposed fix: router should sanitize `x-route-owner` for any internal/background routes and force `route_priority=low` on background embeds. Also add a test asserting `ownership` is never client-propagated for internal route types.
maria: I'd also like console diagnostics: show origin tag on token attribution (toolcall vs background vs background-priority) so ops can quickly filter.
aj: for immediate mitigation: can we gate the background-priority heuristic and backfill provisional charges?
devon: I'm rolling back the gate now. Also will add a sanitizer that strips `x-route-owner` on internal forwards and add unit + integration tests.
maria: thanks. Can we also add a quick script to find other instances where `forwardHeaders` is used for internal routes? Might be more leaks.
sam_k: I'll run a repo grep and a quick query against request traces for the last 48h. If we find matches, I'll open follow-up tickets and a billing reconciliation ticket.
maria: can ops/console team add a temporary dashboard card: "background embed token attribution" (time series of tokens attributed to customer vs system for background routes).
sam_k: yep — I'll add a panel and pin it to the realtime ops dashboard.
irene: note for rollout UX: we should avoid preserving ownership headers by default when promoting features that touch internal routing. Add checklist item to rollout PR template.
devon: adding that to my PR now. Also adding a migration to revoke any provisional charges that matched this exact pattern (cust-1234, background-priority, token_range).
billing-bot: Notice: created billing ticket BILL-842 and flagged provisional charges for review.
maria: thanks everyone — leaving this in incident doc (link: https://go/incident/INC-2026-03-bgembed) and will follow up after rollback + backfill.
aj: small follow-up: should router also set an explicit attribution field (internal_owner = "system") for internal routes to avoid future header-based ambiguity?
irene: yes please. explicit is better than relying on header absence.
devon: agreed. I'll set `internal_owner=system` on any internal forward and make accounting prefer that over headers.
maria: great. ping @sam_k when the dashboard is up and when the reconciliation ticket is created. :thumbsup:
sam_k: will do — ETA 2h for dashboard, creating billing ticket now.
